page: Microsoft Azure E48_v4 is an Ev4-family virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The underlying hardware features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.6 GHz. This configuration provides 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, offering dedicated CPU allocation. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. The processor supports AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), but lacks support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) or SHA extensions. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 199.45 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 94.39 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. The Passmark memory score of 2857.53 also reflects this strong memory subsystem. Conversely, single-threaded performance is a relative bottleneck; gzip compression at 23.41 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 8.89 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression at 189.78 GB/sec and Geekbench multi-core at 11710.0, perform in the average range. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, with prompt processing for a 70B model limited to 6.4 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E48_v4 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. Given the 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and average database operation benchmarks of 17152.51 on Passmark, this server is configured for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise applications requiring large memory footprints. The lack of local storage means data persistence relies entirely on external network-attached storage.
